status_vocabulary.ready: The current validated evidence supports the qualified statement.
status_vocabulary.exploratory_only: Useful mechanism evidence, but not a confirmatory headline.
status_vocabulary.pending_strict_analysis: The design is frozen, but the complete run has not yet passed its fail-closed analyzer.
status_vocabulary.rewrite_required: The planned runs cannot support the statement as currently worded.
status_vocabulary.contradicted: The observed data contain direct counterexamples to the proposed universal statement.

run_snapshot.note: Counts are only a progress snapshot. The analyzers, not file counts, are the completion authority.

claims.defensible_statement: Active probes remain in the target history; passive monitors inspect a copied clean prefix and are discarded.
claims.required_qualification: Signal comparisons are ecological: active scores come from carried trajectories and passive scores from clean trajectories. They are not same-trajectory counterfactuals.

claims.defensible_statement: For active recomputation, 6 of 7 model-by-benchmark success effects are negative; 3 paired 95% intervals exclude zero on the negative side, and one slice is a small positive exception. Active recomputation increases mean total tokens in all 7 slices.
claims.required_qualification: Describe a cross-model trend, not a rule and not a universally significant degradation.

claims.defensible_statement: Equal-format copy, recall, counter, and recomputation arms provide mechanism probes across 5 reasoning models and 4 action models at n=20 per cell.
claims.required_qualification: The success effects are heterogeneous and do not form a monotonic complexity trend. Do not claim that greater chore complexity improves signal quality or monotonically worsens task success.

claims.defensible_statement: There is no universal signal winner. Active recomputation has the highest AUPRC in 3 of 7 confirmatory model-by-benchmark slices; a passive method or context baseline leads the other 4. The useful method therefore depends on model and trace type.
claims.required_qualification: The proposed universal claims 'active is less useful' and 'passive beats baselines' are contradicted by several slices.

claims.defensible_statement: Provider-backed active and passive methods add tokens, latency, and cost; deterministic trace rules, clock, and context-use baselines add no provider calls. Passive observation avoids target-history carry but is not free.
claims.required_qualification: Do not say all passive methods increase token cost; deterministic passive rules do not.

claims.defensible_statement: BFCL supplies action-trace, turn-level failure evidence and genuine early-warning analysis. Evolving Intent supplies verified final success, so its checkpoint signals predict final failure rather than independently graded within-horizon degradation.
claims.required_qualification: Do not describe Evolving Intent precision/recall as turn-level ground truth or as detecting a failure within N turns.

claims.defensible_statement: The observer-effect and signal-quality study covers reasoning traces with Evolving Intent and native tool/action traces with BFCL.
claims.required_qualification: The deployment study is reasoning-only; BFCL is not part of deployment.

claims.defensible_statement_after_gate: On 40 held-out Evolving Intent tasks for Luna, compare 7 online observation methods under no action, lossy compaction, public-state regrounding, and bounded feedback, with paired operator-minus-none effects.
expected_evidence: 1120 exact outputs, jobs, and event logs
One success SVG plus JSON sidecar for the single model-benchmark slice
claims.required_qualification: This is one model on one reasoning benchmark. Natural scalar thresholds produce unequal action rates, so method comparisons combine signal identity and realized firing behavior.

claims.defensible_statement_after_gate: The online feedback operator keeps history and appends a deterministic, bounded WATCH reminder copied exactly from the current user-visible prefix.
claims.required_qualification: It is not LLM-generated, it does not evaluate good versus bad decisions, and the current implementation populates WATCH only.

claims.defensible_statement_after_gate: The primary online study uses calibration-locked scalar thresholds with a one-action cap. A separate frozen two-pass sensitivity yokes four methods to the active anchor schedule.
claims.required_qualification: Primary online interventions are not count-matched. Scalar cutoffs imply 100% task firing for active recomputation, matched frozen recomputation, trace rules, and clock in the pass-one diagnostic; the yoked active anchor therefore acts at checkpoint 1 on all 40 tasks. Treat the two-pass result as an aggressive checkpoint-1 control sensitivity, not a 20% matched-rate estimate.

claims.defensible_statement_after_gate: Report which methods help or hurt Luna on held-out Evolving Intent under each operator, using absolute success and paired operator-minus-none intervals.
claims.required_qualification: Do not generalize the deployment ranking across models, action benchmarks, or all agents. Do not promise that every method has a niche where it wins.

claims.defensible_statement: The powered Evolving core uses DeepSeek V4 Flash, GPT-OSS-120B, GPT-5.6 Luna, and GPT-5.6 Terra; BFCL uses Luna, Terra, and GPT-OSS-120B. Qwen3.7 Plus appears only in exploratory mechanism runs.
claims.required_qualification: Replace Qwen-27B and GPT-4-mini in the exposition; neither is in the powered confirmatory core.

claims.defensible_statement: Each monitored method has an operator=none control trajectory.
claims.required_qualification: There is no unmonitored deployment arm and no oracle deployment bound in either final deployment manifest.

claims.defensible_statement: Signal quality already has one primary precision-recall figure for each of the 7 confirmatory model-by-benchmark slices; observer effects and observer costs have machine-readable SVG sidecars. Online deployment will add one model-by-benchmark success figure; two-pass adds five sensitivity figures.
claims.required_qualification: The planned deployment runs do not provide deployment figures for every confirmatory model-by-benchmark slice.

online_semantic_retry_normalization.scientific_reason: Three passive trace-judge cells required same-prefix semantic recovery after transport-success responses failed strict structured parsing. Passive retries do not enter or advance target history. Every physical attempt must remain in resource accounting.
required_staging_changes: For every affected checkpoint, classify each capped/unparseable physical response as a logical failed attempt without changing provider identity, usage, latency, or cost.
Number the final parseable response as the next logical attempt and map its staged ledger key to the canonical logical request sequence.
Bind every physical call-event ID to the recovered signal so the stock analyzer sums all attempts' tokens, latency, and dollars.
Recompute every dependent staged event/output/job hash without changing a scientific score, decision, task trajectory, or production artifact.
required_receipt_fields: copy-on-write artifact type/version, source run ID, fixed manifest/pair/code hashes, production_inputs_immutable=true, and provider_calls=0
all three recovery receipt paths, artifact types, and SHA256 hashes; exact three-cell/two-source-unit mapping
ordered physical-attempt trail for each normalized logical call, including event IDs, request keys, status, usage, latency, and cost
staged call-attempt and ledger paths/SHA256 hashes plus normalized staged output/job/event/accounting bindings
the single generic unknown-to-failed ledger reconciliation and the exact expected raw-analyzer disagreement
analysis output/path SHA256, 1120 rows, 40 tasks per treatment, 28 treatments, provider_calls=0, and figure hashes
leave-two sensitivity JSON/Markdown hashes, exact two-unit/56-row exclusion, 1064 rows, n=38, and balanced pairing

mandatory_sensitivity.selection: Derive the complete affected-unit set from recovery cells d52046b6eb74a76ecdc3debc, 89df41e0daa1262a43fa5e55, and 786d95760ccdb86713c26936 using only cell_id and unit_id. Require the exact two frozen source units and remove both from all 28 method-operator treatments; any future recovery on a new unit forces an expanded cumulative exclusion.
mandatory_sensitivity.coverage: Recompute all 224 absolute summaries and all 168 operator effects at n=38 with the frozen 2,000-bootstrap/seed-12012 function; the final release audit compares all 21 success effects, all 105 key-resource effects, and every absolute summary against n=40.
mandatory_sensitivity.reporting_rule: The final release inventory reports every point-sign or confidence-interval interpretation change and every material absolute-summary shift under fixed rules.

online_semantic_retry_normalization.paper_disclosure: Three passive judge cells required same-prefix semantic recovery, spanning two of 40 source tasks. Raw logs and the ledger remain unchanged; an analysis-only, hash-bound copy classifies every unparseable response as a logical failed attempt, counts every physical attempt's resources, and is checked with a cumulative paired leave-two-source-task-out sensitivity (n=38).

two_pass_pass_one_recovery.relevance: The final yoked schedule uses active_recompute, frozen_probe:recompute, turn_clock, and context_use, not trace_judge. The warning therefore does not select the four-method schedule, but it remains part of the audit trail.

unsupported_even_after_both_planned_runs: Active observation always harms task success.
Active signals are universally less accurate than passive signals or trivial baselines.
Passive signals universally outperform clock and context baselines.
Observer harm or deployment value is consistent across 4-5 powered models without exceptions.
Increasing active chore complexity monotonically improves detection or worsens observer harm.
Evolving Intent provides independently graded within-N-turn degradation labels.
The deployed feedback is an LLM-generated GOOD/BAD decision critique.
Primary online intervention counts are matched across methods.
Deployment findings generalize across multiple models or to action traces.
The final deployment design includes a truly unmonitored control or an oracle bound.
